intent: A place for pages to land: the web app exists, builds, and talks to the API.
change: packages/web Next.js app: base layout and navigation, typed API client (HTTP only, no DB imports - enforced by lint boundary), environment config, CI build + a smoke page test wired into pnpm check.
done_when: pnpm check builds the web app in CI, the smoke page renders through the dev server, and the lint boundary fails a synthetic direct-DB import.

proofs.claim: The dashboard shell renders through a real Next dev server: the smoke test boots the app in-process on an ephemeral loopback port against a stub API, fetches `/`, and finds the served markup carrying the product name, the Watches, Calendar and Tasks navigation, the Overview heading and the injected API origin - and the page proves it read over HTTP by leaving `/health` in the stub's request log. Stopping twice is safe and genuinely releases the port.

The API is the dashboard's only door, and lint holds it: synthetic dashboard source importing `@chief-of-staff/db`, `@chief-of-staff/db/testing`, `drizzle-orm`, `drizzle-orm/pg-core` or `pg` is refused under the repository's own ESLint configuration, type-only imports included, while `node:crypto` passes - and a negative control proves the rule does not fire outside packages/web. The typed client, its URL joining and its error mapping, and the boot-time environment refusal are proven alongside.

The repository quality gate exits zero with the dashboard in the workspace, and it now builds the dashboard: `scripts/check.mjs` carries a `build:web` step running `next build`, which is what type-checks an application `tsc --build` emits nothing for. The gate is what `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs, so the web build reaches CI without touching the workflow.

intent: The read data the pages need, engine-free and validated at the door.
change: GET /watches/:id/observations (time-bounded series for sparklines) and task list/detail read routes - thin Drizzle queries with JSON-schema validation, cross-user access refused with typed 404.
done_when: Integration tests prove accepted series and task reads against seeded Testcontainers rows, other-user watch returns 404, and malformed queries refuse with typed 4xx.

proofs.claim: The observation series and task reads answer over HTTP against seeded rows: the half-open window and the limit ceiling are honoured in oldest-first order, another user's watch and another user's task are refused with a 404 byte-identical to a nonexistent id, and a malformed bound, an over-ceiling limit, an unknown query key, and an inverted window each refuse with a typed 4xx.
The repository quality gate - lint, both typecheck configs, the unit and integration projects under the coverage thresholds, and the workspace build - exits zero with the new read routes in place.

intent: The dashboard's front door: email in, session out, nothing enumerable.
change: Request-link endpoint with signed single-use expiring tokens, MailerPort with dev/CI link-capture implementation, consume-and-session flow, httpOnly signed cookie, page guard middleware, logout.
done_when: Integration and Playwright tests prove the accepted flow, expired/reused/tampered token refusals, atomic single-use under race, enumeration-safe responses, unauthenticated redirect, and logout.

proofs.claim: Before the flow exists, the composed path already runs end to end and stops at exactly one seam: the integration suite boots the real Fastify server against a seeded database, posts a link request, and reaches `registerAuthRoutes`, which is not implemented yet. The failure is the unimplemented route registration rather than a missing file or a broken harness.

Before the guard exists, the dashboard's own composed path runs and stops at one seam: the e2e boots the Next dev server, requests a guarded page, and the middleware reaches `readSession`, which is not implemented yet.

The magic-link flow answers over HTTP against a seeded database: a link request hands the MailerPort a single-use link for a seeded address, consuming it issues an httpOnly session cookie, and the refusals are each observable and side-effect-free - an expired token, an already-consumed token and a tampered token are all refused, two concurrent consumptions of the same token authenticate at most one, and a request for an unknown address answers byte-identically to a known one so no account can be enumerated. Logout ends the session.

A real browser walks the dashboard's front door: Playwright drives the Next dev server against the live API and a seeded database, is redirected from a guarded page to the request-link page while unauthenticated, requests a link, follows the captured link, lands on the dashboard rendering its own user's data, and after logout is redirected away again. A garbage session cookie is treated as unauthenticated rather than as an error page.

The repository quality gate - lint, both typecheck configs, the unit and integration projects under the coverage thresholds, the workspace build and the dashboard build - exits zero with magic-link auth, its migration and the page guard in place.

intent: The page that shows the product working: every watch, its history, and a pause switch.
change: Watches page: list with status and last observation, observation sparkline component fed by the series route, pause/resume control calling the CRUD route, empty state.
done_when: Playwright e2e against seeded Testcontainers proves rendered rows and sparkline match the seed, pause round-trips and re-renders, empty seed renders the empty state, and cross-user rows never appear.

proofs.claim: Before the page exists, its whole composed path already runs and stops at exactly one seam: the e2e seeds a database with two users' watches and observations, boots the real API and the real Next dev server, signs a browser in through a real magic link, opens `/watches`, and the page's server component reaches `loadWatchesView`, which is not implemented yet. The failure is that one unimplemented loader rather than a missing route, an unseeded database or a browser that never signed in.

The watches page renders exactly the seeded facts, in a browser, against the real API: every watch the signed-in user owns with its status and its last observation, a sparkline whose plotted points are that watch's seeded observation series in seeded order, and none of the other user's watches. Pausing a watch from the page round-trips through the CRUD route and the re-rendered page shows the new status. An account with nothing seeded gets the designed empty state rather than a blank page. What a browser cannot provoke against a healthy API - an unreachable server, a refused list, a refused series - is proven against the loader directly in `packages/web/src/watches/view-model.test.ts`, which this argv does not run and the gate does.

The repository quality gate - lint, both typecheck configs, the unit and integration projects under the coverage thresholds, the workspace build and the dashboard build - exits zero with the watches page, its observation-series client method and its pause control in place, including the third suite in the run that boots a Next dev server.

intent: The calendar and task surfaces s5 and s7 will build on.
change: Calendar page (upcoming items by date with deadline/renewal badges) and task history shell page (task rows from the read routes), empty states, API-error states for all three pages.
done_when: Playwright e2e proves both pages render seeded rows and empty states, the task shell links reserve the s5 detail slot, and a simulated API failure renders the visible error state.

proofs.claim: Before either loader exists, the whole composed path already runs and stops at exactly the two functions this task is for. The e2e seeds a database with two accounts' calendar items and task histories, boots the real API and the real Next dev server, signs a browser in through a real magic link, and opens `/calendar` - where the page's server component reaches `loadCalendarView`, which is not implemented. The failure is that unimplemented loader rather than a missing route, an unseeded database, a fixture that cannot plant a calendar item, or a browser that never signed in.

Both pages render exactly the seeded facts, in a browser, against the real API. The calendar files every row under its own date soonest first - which the API cannot have handed it, because `GET /calendar-items` answers in name order and the seed's name order disagrees with its date order at every position - labels a deadline and a renewal differently, prints an amount only where one was recorded, and shows an undated row rather than dropping it. The task history lists every run newest first with its status, and each row links to `/tasks/<the seeded id>`, which is the detail slot s5 fills. Neither page shows another account's rows, and an account with nothing seeded gets the designed empty state on both. Finally, with the dashboard pointed at a port nothing is listening on, all three pages - watches, calendar and tasks - render their error state naming the cause, and draw normally again once the API is back. The outage half of that claim also proves the guard: with the API gone the middleware can no longer verify the session it is holding, and rather than bouncing the browser to a sign-in page that needs the same dead API to send a link, it lets the request through to the page that can say what happened. Nothing is disclosed by that, because every fact on every one of these pages arrives through the API that is not answering.

The repository quality gate - lint, both typecheck configs, the unit and integration projects under the coverage thresholds, the workspace build and the dashboard build - exits zero with the calendar and task pages in place, including the fourth suite in the run that boots a Next dev server. The ordering, labelling and formatting decisions the browser proves through the rendered page are also proven directly against the loaders in `packages/web/src/calendar/view-model.test.ts` and `packages/web/src/tasks/view-model.test.ts`, which this gate runs and the e2e argv does not.
